correctness.rationale: For every selected (i,j), the exact outside-neighbor count is n-rho_i+m-kappa_j. A dominating set cannot have both an empty row and empty column. If all rows are covered, rho_i>=max(1,n-k) for each row because every selected cell satisfies rho_i+kappa_j>=m+n-k with kappa_j<=m; similarly when all columns are covered. Taking the smaller bound and matching it by complete column/row slabs proves the all-parameter identity. Equality in the bound forces every used column or row to be full when 1<=k<min(m,n), yielding the exhaustive optimizer classification and counts. The separately coded brute-force checker tested all 1,763,138 nonempty candidate subsets across 14 boards, all 93 capacity cases, and equality counts, with zero disagreements. No finite test is used as an infinite certificate.

originality.rationale: In the materially read first version of Tepeh, arXiv:2606.22428, Theorem 7 is a general upper bound for products and Proposition 8 gives equality only for the diagonal pair K_{k+2} square K_{k+2}. The present theorem requires a new matching lower bound for all m,n and separately classifies every minimum set for 1<=k<min(m,n). The origin paper arXiv:2606.22422 covers the definition and complete graph values, not this product theorem. Searches for the equivalent regular-graph (1,t)-domination formulation and published-finding corpus records showed no statement implying this exact result. Full access to the October 2026 revised text was unavailable and is a declared nonzero literature risk.

value.rationale: The parameter was introduced in June 2026 and the immediate motivating Cartesian-product study specifically isolates rook graphs as sharpness witnesses while proving only the K_{k+2} square case. This theorem settles exact equality of the product upper bound on the entire canonical three-parameter family, including arbitrarily rectangular factors, and classifies every optimum in the nontrivial low-capacity regime. The coverage dichotomy and rigidity are structural information, not an arbitrary finite computation or a mere restatement of the existing upper bound. It does not claim a solution for all product graphs or a classification of high-capacity minimizers.
